s1.syndrome_frame: Acute collapse with recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
salient_findings: Repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology
Recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Collapsed at home and received chest compressions from her husband
Recovered consciousness at home
Vital signs were normal on admission
Physical examination was unremarkable
ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals
ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes
Short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds
Continuous ECG monitoring revealed recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Some episodes deteriorated into ventricular fibrillation
Serum electrolyte levels were normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure
Emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease
Genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, normal cardiac function and structure, and genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Normal cardiac function and structure, normal serum electrolyte levels, and no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Early repolarization syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals, and repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes

shortlist.label: Familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, and genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)

shortlist.label: Short-coupled polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds and recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with a short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds, which is characteristic of short-coupled polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation (SC-PMVT/VF). Additionally, the patient experienced recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that deteriorated into ventricular fibrillation, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: Although the patient experienced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, there is no mention of the episodes being triggered by physical activity or emotional stress, which is typical of CPVT.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: The patient's ECG showed specific abnormalities, including repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes, which suggests a more specific diagnosis than idiopathic ventricular fibrillation.

rejected.label: Early repolarization syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG did not show the characteristic J-point elevation or ST-segment elevation seen in early repolarization syndrome.

rejected.label: Familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: There is no mention of a family history of similar conditions, which would be expected in familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
